name: King of Ivvah
overview: The King of Ivvah is a male monarch mentioned in the Bible who is noted for having been defeated by Assyria. No specific tribal affiliation or additional personal details are provided in Scripture. His role is primarily defined by his political defeat as recorded in 2 Kings 19:13.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Ivvah' literally means 'king of Ivvah' and is used as a straightforward designation rather than a personal name. It is not a name given by God but a descriptive title identifying his rulership over the region of Ivvah, as referenced in 2 Kings 19:13.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of Ivvah beyond what is mentioned in his unique attribute as a defeated king. There are no additional familial or relational details provided.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Ivvah is significant in the biblical narrative as an example of the nations subdued by Assyria during its expansion. His defeat illustrates the power of Assyria and sets the historical and theological context for the challenges faced by Israel and Judah. This reference serves to highlight God's sovereignty over the nations and the unfolding of His purposes in history.
